description: The version 2 pool, in the pool.json case shape (see its description), for a file that says formatVersion 2. Two fields are added. filters, when present, is the rules file's filters object (genres, years, kind; an empty object is allowed); absent means none. The runtime part of filters is left out here: it is applied where the epoch's pool is cut (The pool of an epoch), not by the pool evaluator, and lineup-v2.json covers it. films, in every case, is the film-to-collection map of Groups in version 2 for this pool: each movie of the pool that is a member movie of a collection named in sources (a collection source) and present in the snapshot, mapped to that collection's ID, the smallest such ID (32 ASCII bytes, unsigned) when there are several; an empty object when none. Only rotation and a capped shuffle read the map; it is given here whatever the mode. Sources and exclusions may use type item.
source: Computed with an independent Python reference written from docs/rules-format.md only (Items and the pool, Sources, Exclusions, Filters, Maximum rating and the rating ladder, String matching, Groups in version 2), without reading any Kotlin. The reference script is not committed, as for the version 1 vectors; it reproduces every case of pool.json and of rating.json's ladder, normalise and eligibility tables. Item IDs are synthetic.

cases.name: filters genres: any of the names passes
filters genres: an episode takes its series' genres; with its series missing it uses its own names only
cases.note: Series ...0399 and ...0398 are not in the snapshot. As for a genre source, the filter is not fail-closed: ...0203 passes on its own genre, ...0204 has none and fails. ...0205 and ...0206 are loose episodes.

cases.name: filters genres: names are matched as String matching says (ASCII letters fold, nothing else)
cases.note: é and É are not ASCII and do not fold; a trailing space is not trimmed.

cases.name: filters years: from and to both included; an item with no production year fails
cases.note: The episode ...0201 has no production year of its own; a year is never taken from the series.

cases.name: filters years: a single-year range
filters kind movie
filters kind episode: series episodes and loose episodes
filters: an empty filters object changes nothing
filters: every part must pass (genres AND years AND kind)
cases.note: ...0101 is a movie; ...0202 is out of the years; ...0203's series is Drama.

cases.name: filters AND the rating ceiling: an item has to pass both
cases.note: ...0102 is over the ceiling; ...0103 fails the years; ...0104 is unrated (fails closed); ...0202's series is TV-MA.

cases.name: filters come after the exclusions: an excluded item that passes the filters stays out, and a second source does not bring back an item a filter rejects
item source: adds one movie and one episode to the union
item exclusion: removes one episode from a series source
item source: an ID not in the snapshot, or naming a series, a collection or a library, matches nothing
item exclusion: an unknown ID removes nothing, and an item exclusion does not fail closed
cases.note: Series ...0399 is not in the snapshot. The item exclusion is decided by the ID alone: it removes ...0201 and leaves ...0202.

cases.name: item source and item exclusion of the same ID: the exclusion wins
item source: the rating ceiling still applies to a picked item
cases.note: ...0201's series ...0399 is not in the snapshot, so under a ceiling it fails closed, even when picked by ID.

cases.name: item source with a genre filter: a picked item still has to pass the filters
films map: a film in two named collections maps to the smaller collection ID
cases.note: The larger ID is listed first in sources and in collections: the order does not matter, the smaller 32-hex ID wins.

cases.name: films map: the smaller ID is compared as bytes (a digit sorts before a letter)
films map: a film in a named and an unnamed collection maps to the named one, even when the unnamed ID is smaller
cases.note: Collection ...04a1 is in the snapshot but is not a source: it groups nothing, so ...0102 (in the pool through the library) is not in the map.

cases.name: films map: a collection of shows maps no films; episodes keep their series
films map: only member movies are grouped; a member episode in the same collection is not
films map: films outside the pool are not in the map (excluded, filtered out, over the ceiling)
films map: a film that entered the pool through another source is still grouped by a named collection
films map: a named collection that is not in the snapshot groups nothing (and selects nothing)
films map: a collection that is only an exclusion groups nothing; a named collection with a film the exclusion removes
films map: a collection that is both a source and an exclusion contributes nothing and maps nothing
